evals.prompt: We run the marketing for Καρράς Ηλεκτρολογικές Εργασίες (karras-electric.gr), an electrician in Piraeus. Our US parent agency sent over its local-services playbook, which tells every office: 'launch Local Services Ads to get the Google Screened badge above everything, and target the featured snippet for your head keyword.' Before we spend anything, our team captured the actual Greek SERP — it's in evals/files/serp-snapshot-ilektrologos-peiraias-el.md, and it is all the data we have (no tools connected). Map the SERP features per your taxonomy, give us the feature strategy for «ηλεκτρολόγος πειραιάς», and tell us straight how the LSA and featured-snippet advice fits the Greek market.
evals.expected_output: A feature-mapping and strategy report built solely from the 2026-08-05 Piraeus capture: composition mapped exactly (ads, Local Pack, PAA, related searches present; snippet/AI Overview and the rest recorded absent for this pull), the US playbook corrected for Greece — LSA stated unavailable in Greece per the taxonomy's el-GR census and not recommended, kept distinct from the organic Local Pack strategy the fixture supports (GBP completeness plus reviews benchmarked against the observed 212/89/301-review pack occupants) — snippet/AI Overview pursuit framed as confirm-per-keyword on live el-GR SERPs, local-commercial intent evidenced from the composition, and every metric labeled user-provided/manual observation or estimated, since no tool data exists.
expectations: SERP composition is mapped fixture-exactly per the Output Validation item 'SERP composition mapped with all features documented': every feature the fixture inventory marks observed (3 text ads, the 3-listing Local Pack between organic #2 and #3, the 4 PAA questions, related searches) is identified, and every feature the inventory marks 'Not observed' (featured snippet, AI Overview, knowledge panel, image pack, video, shopping, sitelinks, LSA unit) is reported as absent on this pull — recorded as an observation of this 2026-08-05 capture, not as a permanent property of the query — with no feature reported present that the fixture does not show.

The playbook's LSA advice is corrected per the taxonomy's 'Greece (el-GR) availability' annotation at §7: the response states that Local Services Ads is not available in Greece (the census's owner-verified finding — Greece is not listed in the LSA country picker) and does NOT recommend launching LSA or pursuing the 'Google Screened' badge for this Greek client; it keeps LSA (a paid unit, unavailable in Greece) distinct from the organic Local Pack (observed present in the fixture and actionable). A response that recommends LSA spend for the Greek market, or that conflates the two units, fails; noting the LSA-to-Google-Ads migration re-check is a plus, not required.

Local Pack strategy follows the taxonomy §7 playbook and cites the fixture's specific data points per 'Every recommendation cites specific data points (not generic advice)': entering the pack via the client's existing verified GBP ('Claim and optimize Google Business Profile — Complete every field' — the fixture shows Products/Services empty and the last owner post 14 months ago) and review building ('Collect and respond to reviews — Volume and recency of reviews matter') benchmarked against the observed pack occupants (4,9/212 · 4,7/89 · 4,4/301 vs the client's 11 reviews) — at least the GBP-completeness and review levers appear with those fixture numbers; citations/NAP consistency and LocalBusiness schema are plus items.

el-GR census discipline on features not in this pull: the playbook's featured-snippet advice is handled evidence-first — the response records that no featured snippet (and no AI Overview) was observed on this capture, does not promise winning a snippet on a SERP that currently displays none, and frames any snippet or AI Overview pursuit as confirm-per-keyword on live el-GR SERPs, consistent with the taxonomy's locale note ('absence of an annotation means "unknown for Greece," not "available in Greece"') and its §3 el-GR note ('record AI Overview presence per keyword during the audit rather than assuming the general trigger patterns above hold for Greek queries'). Unconditioned 'target the featured snippet' advice presented as an available lever for this query fails.

Intent and ranking-pattern analysis is derived from the fixture per 'Ranking factors identified from actual top 10 analysis (not assumptions)': primary intent identified as local/commercial service intent with the composition evidence named (ads + Local Pack + the aggregator/directory-heavy organic top 10 — positions 1, 2, 7, 8), and the strategy reflects the observed pattern (e.g. the client homepage at #9 competing against aggregators, and the content opportunity evidenced by the #5 cost guide plus the fixture's cost/certification PAA questions). The capture's date, location, and device are carried into the report per the Input Validation items 'SERP data is current (date confirmed)' and 'Search location and device type confirmed'.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every position, domain, business name, rating, review count, ad, and PAA question in the analysis traces to the fixture; no search volumes, CTRs, DA/backlink values, or SERP-share figures appear as measured data (the fixture states none exist) — if the difficulty template's DA/backlink fields are used they carry 'estimated' or an explained N/A — and each data point's source is labeled per 'Source of each data point clearly stated (~~SEO tool data, ~~AI monitor data, user-provided, or manual observation)', with nothing presented as tool-fetched.

evals.prompt: Έχουμε το e-shop «Ηλεκτρική Αγορά» (ilektriki-agora.gr) με μικροσυσκευές. Μαζέψαμε μόνοι μας ό,τι βλέπουμε στο Google και στο Skroutz για τη σκούπα ρομπότ Vektra R30 — όλα τα στοιχεία είναι στο evals/files/skroutz-vektra-r30-el.md· δεν έχουμε συνδεδεμένα εργαλεία. Θέλουμε πλήρη ανάλυση ορατότητας (Google και Skroutz) με προτεραιότητες. Και για το business case: (α) πόσο είναι σήμερα το τέλος Skoop ανά παραγγελία; (β) πόσα lockers έχει τώρα η BoxNow; (γ) ποιο ποσοστό ακυρώσεων ανέχεται το Skroutz πριν επιβάλει κύρωση; (δ) ο οικονομικός μας διευθυντής διάβασε ότι το BestPrice είναι «το Νο1 site σύγκρισης τιμών στην Ελλάδα» — μήπως να μεταφέρουμε εκεί το βάρος από το Skroutz; Γράψε την ανάλυση στα ελληνικά.
evals.expected_output: A Greek-language visibility analysis with Google and Skroutz as clearly separated sections: fixture-grounded findings (the 3 missing filter attributes, the shipping-inclusive price benchmark against the identical-SKU listings, the 4-of-6 locker gap, the stale 38-review base vs the 412-review category leader, the 14-vs-10-day returns mismatch flagged as a compliance red flag, and the missing Merchant Center feed with free listings correctly treated as live for Greece), every Skroutz ranking-effect statement framed as an observable, unconfirmed lever, the Skoop-fee/locker-count/SLA questions answered with zero invented figures and routed to current Skroutz primary sources, and the BestPrice «Νο1» claim bounded as a vendor category-label quirk — never 'BestPrice out-trafficks Skroutz' — with Google organic + Skroutz kept first as an effort-ordering heuristic.
expectations: Surface separation per SKILL.md: Skroutz findings appear as a clearly separated section from the Google SERP analysis — 'they are different, independently unpublished algorithms; do not merge their ranking-factor lists' — and the analysis never explains the client's Skroutz position by Google ranking factors or vice versa; if the Shopping unit or BestPrice get recommendations, those are likewise reported per surface (greek-shopping-surfaces §4, 'Report per surface, separately').

The audit works the fixture's observable levers with the fixture's own numbers, not generic advice: (a) the 3 named empty filter attributes («χωρητικότητα κάδου», «αυτονομία», «λειτουργία σφουγγαρίσματος») tied to filtered-search eligibility; (b) price benchmarked against the identical-SKU listings on a stated shipping basis (289 € + 4,90 € vs 279 € + 3,90 €), not against a category average; (c) the locker gap (BoxNow pickup appears on 4 of the 6 shops listing the SKU and not on the client's listing — the client is one of the 2 without it; a fixture-true restatement such as '4 of the client's 5 competitors offer it' also passes); (d) the review gap (4,6/5 from 38, newest 5 months old, rare replies — vs the category leader's 4,8/5 from 412 with weekly reviews and seller responses); (e) the returns mismatch (14 days declared in the seller panel vs 10 days on the site) flagged in the checklist's own terms as a compliance red flag, not just an SEO issue; and (f) the Merchant Center gap — the fixture's Shopping unit shows the R30 on two competitor cards and none from the client — with free product listings treated as live/supported for Greece (a zero-cost surface), never described as unavailable or paid-only.

W6 claim-tag discipline (docs/loop/WATCH-ITEMS.md): every ranking-effect statement about Skroutz is framed as an observable lever — directional and unconfirmed — per the reference's 'observable levers … not a table of confirmed ranking weights': whether price rank influences the default/relevance sort is presented as not confirmed by Skroutz (the 5th-of-6 default-sort position may be cited as an observation, never as proof of mechanism); the delivery-badge question as ranking input vs buyer-trust signal as 'not confirmed either way'; Trusted Reviews as a program that exists and gates status while its ranking weight is not published; the attribute-gap effect with direction understood but 'magnitude is not published'. Any Skroutz factor asserted as a confirmed weight or percentage fails.

The three magnitude questions are answered without inventing a single figure (W6 open claims): no Skoop fee amount, no current BoxNow locker count, and no cancellation-rate/SLA threshold appears as a number anywhere in the response — each is named an open/unverified item to resolve 'against current help.skroutz.gr or Skroutz seller-panel documentation before making client-facing claims, especially on figures (fees, locker counts, SLA thresholds)'; the Skoop fee may be described as reported in effect since 01 Dec 2025 and is treated as a competitive-cost input, not a ranking factor; the ~300k BoxNow figure, if it appears at all, appears only as the reported end-2026 target (reported 12 Jul 2026) that must be re-verified before citing to a client — never as a current count or established fact.

W9 vendor-magnitude bounding on the BestPrice question: the «Νο1» claim is explained as a vendor category-listing label (SimilarWeb's Greek price-comparison category, in which Skroutz is simply not listed), the response does not tell the client BestPrice out-trafficks Skroutz, and any SimilarWeb visit figures cited (~6.9M / ~40.8M per month) are labeled vendor-measured estimates with their Apr/Jun 2026 snapshot dating — never audited fact; prioritization keeps Google organic + Skroutz first as the reference's effort-ordering heuristic ('This is an effort-ordering heuristic, not a traffic-share claim') rather than shifting weight to BestPrice, and BestPrice work, if suggested, is the presence-and-quality check of greek-shopping-surfaces §1.

Greek output quality (watch-item W4 guard, docs/loop/WATCH-ITEMS.md), mechanically checkable layer only: correct diacritics and final-sigma use throughout, and no untranslated English boilerplate headings (platform and product names such as Skroutz, BoxNow, Merchant Center, Vektra R30 may stay in Latin script). Fluency, idiomatic naturalness, translation-ese, and e-commerce register are judged by the binding greek-content-editor pass this eval's Greek prose output is flagged for at Mode B time — that pass, not this expectation, issues the naturalness verdict; this expectation covers only the layer gradable from the text alone.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every number, name, rating, position, and policy detail in the analysis traces to the fixture or the prompt; no competitor costs (the fixture says none are accessible), no traffic or conversion figures, no invented Skroutz penalties or mechanics, and no business-case arithmetic built on unverified fees appear as findings; open-question caveats live in the analysis prose where the decision is made (ledger F13 placement discipline), and anything the data cannot answer is named as data to obtain, never filled in.

evals.prompt: We're the content team at HeatNest (boiler cover plans, heatnest.co.uk). Target keyword: 'how often should a boiler be serviced'. Everything we captured plus the values from our own Ahrefs export are in evals/files/serp-snapshot-boiler-service-en.md — no tools are connected in this session, so that file is the entire data set. Give us the full SERP analysis: composition, why the top pages rank, the feature strategy (we want the featured snippet and an AI Overview citation), intent, realistic difficulty for our domain, and the recommended content plan.
evals.expected_output: A full SERP analysis of the boiler-service capture: composition mapped exactly with the AI Overview + featured snippet co-occurrence read as the high-information combination, a paragraph-format snippet strategy targeting the observed holder, an AI Overview citation strategy derived from the four cited sources' why-cited patterns, all four PAA questions mapped into the content plan as exact-question headings with concise answers, informational intent and ranking patterns (2026-refresh freshness, guide-format dominance, the DA-31 outlier at #6) drawn from the fixture table, difficulty placed against HeatNest's DA 42 with the Ahrefs-export values labeled as user-provided tool data — and the metrics the export lacks (backlinks, volumes, CTR) marked estimated or N/A, never invented.
expectations: SERP composition is mapped fixture-exactly per 'SERP composition mapped with all features documented' — AI Overview (summary-paragraph format) on top, 2 text ads, the paragraph featured snippet, the 4-question PAA, related searches, and the features the inventory marks not observed reported as absent on this pull — and the AI Overview + featured snippet co-occurrence is read per the taxonomy's combination table ('Google sees this as high-information query' → 'Optimize for both'), with both features addressed in the strategy.

Featured-snippet strategy follows the taxonomy §1 playbook anchored to the fixture's snippet: the current holder (warmhomehub.co.uk/boiler-service-guide) and sub-type (paragraph) are identified from the fixture, and the winning strategy matches that observed format — 'Match the existing format', a concise 40-60-word paragraph answer placed immediately after a heading matching the query — rather than proposing a list or table snippet this SERP does not display.

AI Overview citation strategy is grounded in the fixture's four cited sources and their why-cited notes (definition · safety-requirement wording · step-by-step list · cost figures — mapping onto the §3 Source Citation Patterns rows for definitions, step-by-step processes, and statistics), and recommends at least two §3 playbook behaviors (e.g. 'Write clear, citable sentences', 'Front-load key information', structured data, original data and statistics). No AI Overview citation-rate, trigger-rate, or traffic statistic is invented — the fixture contains none.

PAA strategy covers all four fixture questions per the §2 playbook: each is mapped into the content plan using the exact question as an H2 or H3 with a direct, concise answer per 'Keep answers concise (40-60 words)'; FAQ schema may be suggested per that playbook (this suite does not grade rich-result-eligibility claims either way); questions beyond the fixture's four may be proposed only as suggested coverage (e.g. from related searches), never presented as questions observed on this SERP.

Intent, ranking patterns, and difficulty come from the fixture's top-10 table per 'Ranking factors identified from actual top 10 analysis (not assumptions)': informational intent evidenced from the composition (AI Overview + snippet + PAA, no shopping/local features); observed patterns named from the table (e.g. 2026-updated freshness across most of the top 5, guide/how-to format dominance, the DA range 31-71 with the DA-31 local installer at #6 called out as the outlier/attainability evidence per Tip 5, 'Study the outliers'); and a realistic difficulty read that places HeatNest's DA 42 within the template's site tiers (new/growing/established), with the DA and word-count inputs labeled as the user's Ahrefs export per 'Source of each data point clearly stated (~~SEO tool data, ~~AI monitor data, user-provided, or manual observation)'.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard) with F13 placement awareness: every position, URL, DA value, word count, and date traces to the fixture; metrics the export lacks (backlinks, referring domains, search volume, CTR) appear only as explicitly estimated values or explained N/A — never as measured numbers; and if the content plan proposes a paste-ready title or H1 string, that string carries no bracketed data-needed tokens (bracketed slots inside outline scaffolding are fine — the guarded surface is copy offered as final), with any gaps flagged in the report prose instead.

evals.prompt: I own Aiolos Suites, a 12-room boutique hotel in Naxos. My marketing assistant captured one Google results page — it's in evals/files/hotel-serp-naxos-single-pull-en.md, and it is genuinely all the data we have (no tools connected, no Search Console export on this machine). From this I'd like: (1) our 12-month seasonality calendar so we know when to publish next year's content; (2) the CTR we'd get at position 3 and roughly how many bookings that traffic would mean; (3) whether the DMA changes are why our direct bookings fell — I read free-booking-link clicks are down 30%; (4) what we should actually do to show up more. Also, about a third of our guests are German — do we need anything separate for them?
evals.expected_output: An honest split between what the single Naxos pull shows and what it cannot: fixture-exact mapping with capture metadata carried (hotel-unit shape, the official-site link observation, the 2-of-10 direct-site headroom count, the client at #14), a measurement plan instead of an asserted seasonality calendar, an explicit statement that CTR/traffic/bookings cannot be derived from one snapshot, the '30% free-booking-link' figure bounded as vendor-reported and directional (not confirmed as the cause of the booking drop), separate DE/EL keyword sets and SERP pulls recommended per the language-split rule, and TripAdvisor/Booking framed as observable levers to audit — with no invented volumes, standings, CTRs, or month curves anywhere.
expectations: The analysis extracts what the single pull CAN show, fixture-exactly and with metadata: the hotel unit's observed shape (4 named property cards, date-picker and price filter, the 'Official site' link seen on the one expanded panel) recorded as observations of this pull; the direct-vs-OTA headroom measured per the tourism reference §2 checklist ('Direct hotel/property sites in the top 10? Count them — this measures direct-vs-OTA headroom for the query') as 2 of 10, with the client's own site noted at position 14; and the SERP observations carrying the capture's date, location, language, and device per 'Every hotel-SERP observation must carry capture date, location setting, and language — an undated hotel-SERP snapshot is unusable in this flux period.'

Seasonality honest-gap (§4, 'Measure, Don't Assume'): no 12-month calendar is asserted from this snapshot — the response states that one SERP capture cannot yield demand seasonality ('month patterns differ by destination, origin market, and product — do not assert a month curve as fact in any report') and instead lays out the measurement plan: per-month search volumes for 24+ months per keyword (~~SEO tool, or Google Trends with its relative-index caveat noted), measured peak/shoulder/trough marking, lead-time measurement, movable dates (e.g. Orthodox Easter). Any month named as a likely peak is framed as an assumption to be measured, never as a finding of this analysis ('A calendar row without a source and date is an assumption, not a finding').

CTR/traffic honest-gap: the response states that position-3 CTR, traffic, and bookings cannot be derived from a single SERP snapshot and names the data that would answer them (search-volume data, Search Console impressions/CTR, rank tracking, booking analytics); no CTR percentage, visit count, or bookings number appears as a measured or fixture-derived figure — a generic industry CTR curve may be mentioned only if explicitly labeled a generic estimate not derived from this data, and an unlabeled number fails (ledger F3 class).

W9 vendor-magnitude bounding on the DMA question (docs/loop/WATCH-ITEMS.md): the user's '30%' is identified as a vendor-reported figure, not engine-primary — 'Directional at best; never quote to a client unverified' — so it is not confirmed back to the user as fact and not presented as the established cause of the client's direct-bookings drop (which the fixture contains no data to diagnose); the hotel-SERP flux is handled per §2 ('hotel-SERP layout in Greece is unstable — evidence-first, capture per audit, assume nothing'): the free-booking-link sighting stays a this-pull observation, the layout is not generalized, and re-capture per audit/query is recommended.

Language-split discipline (§5): the response flags that this pull covers only one market-language pair (English, London) and recommends separate keyword sets and separate SERP pulls for the German market (and the EL domestic set if pursued) per 'Treat them as separate SERPs: separate keyword sets, separate SERP pulls, separate difficulty scores' — anchored to the client's stated guest mix (about a third German) rather than an assumed origin-market ranking; the London pull's composition is not extrapolated to DE or EL SERPs.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): OTA domains, positions, property names and scores, and PAA questions all trace to the fixture; TripAdvisor/Booking recommendations (their fixture presence at positions #1, #2, #9 may be cited) are framed as the §3 observable levers to audit — claim status, review volume and recency vs same-destination competitors, response rate, position within the platform's own destination lists — never as assumed current standings, invented ratings, or platform ranking weights; and if Greek-tourism market context is invoked, GDP figures are not converted into search-volume or SERP-share claims (§1).

evals.prompt: What does the Google SERP for 'emergency dentist manchester' look like right now — which practices rank, is there a map pack, is there an AI Overview, and how hard is it to break in? No tools are connected and I haven't sent you any screenshots or exports; just tell me from what you know.
evals.expected_output: The response declines to describe an unseen SERP: it states it cannot analyze without SERP data and does not pretend to fetch it, fabricates no composition, rankings, feature presence, or difficulty score for 'emergency dentist manchester', requests the skill's manual inputs (SERP screenshot or detailed description, top-10 URLs, location and device, capture date), explains the evidence-first reason in the skill's own terms, and at most offers typical-pattern hypotheses explicitly labeled for verification plus the framework it will run once data arrives.
expectations: No SERP is fabricated: the response presents no current SERP composition, no feature-presence claims (Local Pack, ads, featured snippet, AI Overview), no named ranking practices or domains, no positions, and no difficulty score as observations or findings for this query — no data was supplied and none can be fetched. Typical-pattern statements (e.g. that emergency/near-me service queries commonly trigger a Local Pack) pass only when explicitly labeled as expectations or assumptions to verify against the live SERP — hedging words alone ('probably', 'usually shows') are not such a label (keyword-research suite precedent) — and a mocked-up example SERP passes only if unmistakably labeled hypothetical.

No fake tool reads (ledger F3 guard): the response does not claim to have checked, fetched, or seen the live SERP (phrasings like 'the SERP currently shows…' or 'I checked and…' fail); if a live fetch was attempted and failed, the failure is reported as such and no fetched-looking content substitutes for it.

The manual-data mode is engaged per SKILL.md ('Ask the user to provide: 1. Target keyword(s) to analyze 2. SERP screenshots or detailed descriptions of search results 3. URLs of top 10 ranking pages 4. Search location and device type (mobile/desktop) 5. Any observations about SERP features (featured snippets, PAA, AI Overviews)'): the response requests at minimum the SERP screenshot or detailed description, the location and device, and the capture date per the Input Validation item 'SERP data is current (date confirmed)'.

The hold is grounded and forward-moving, not a bare refusal: the response explains why analysis without SERP data would violate the skill's evidence rules (Tip 1: 'Always check SERP before writing - Don't assume, verify'; Output Validation: 'Ranking factors identified from actual top 10 analysis (not assumptions)') and states exactly what unblocks the analysis; offering the analysis framework or a capture checklist while waiting is acceptable and does not fail.
